entries.canonical_text: Applying any of the following iterative pruning techniques—global unstructured magnitude pruning, $L_1$-based unstructured magnitude pruning, $L_2$-based structured magnitude pruning, $L_\infty$-based structured magnitude pruning, random structured pruning, and random unstructured pruning—to replicas of the same base neural network with identical random initialization, and following the experimental training/pruning protocol used here (stochastic gradient descent for 30 epochs per pruning round, constant learning rate 0.01, batch size 32, 20% of remaining parameters pruned per iteration, and rewinding unpruned weights to their initialization before the next iteration), yields multiple distinct sparse sub-networks that retrain to comparable test accuracy at similar overall sparsity levels on the evaluated image-classification datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Kuzushiji-MNIST, EMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN) and architectures (LeNet, AlexNet, VGG11, ResNet18).

entries.canonical_text: For SGD-trained VGG11 on CIFAR-100 that is sparsified and rewound to its initial weight values after each pruning iteration, test accuracy under seven pruning techniques (L2-structured, global unstructured, L1-unstructured, L2-structured, L∞-structured, random structured, and random unstructured) remains near its unpruned level until roughly 70–90% of the weights are pruned, after which it collapses sharply toward near-zero values at the highest pruning fractions, with some techniques degrading earlier than others.

entries.canonical_text: For LeNet on FashionMNIST, test accuracy of SGD-trained, sparsified models that were rewound to initial weight values after each pruning iteration generally decreased as the fraction of pruned weights increased from 0.20 to 0.99, and the seven pruning techniques (L2-structured, global unstructured, L1-unstructured, L1-structured, L∞-structured, random structured, and random unstructured) showed distinct degradation profiles, with some maintaining higher accuracy at high pruning fractions than others.
